ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AD \parallel BC\), \(\angle BAD=90^\circ\), and diagonals \(BD \perp DC\), \(AD=4\), \(BC=9\), what is the length of \(BD\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AD \parallel BC$ and $BD \perp DC$, \\
$\therefore \angle ADB = \angle DBC$, and $\angle BDC = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAD = \angle BDC = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \triangle ADB \sim \triangle DBC$, \\
$\therefore \frac{AD}{BD} = \frac{BD}{BC}$, \\
$\therefore BD^{2} = AD \cdot BC = 4 \times 9 = 36$, \\
$\therefore BD = \boxed{6}$ (negative values are discarded).

Therefore \(\angle BAD = \angle BDC = 90^\circ\), so \(\triangle ADB \sim \triangle DBC\). Therefore \(\frac{AD}{BD} = \frac{BD}{BC}\), so \(BD^2 = AD \cdot BC = 4 \times 9 = 36\). Therefore \(BD = \boxed{6}\) (negative values are discarded).

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is quadrilateral ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, D is to the right of A and roughly on the same horizontal line as A, C is to the right of B and roughly on the same horizontal line as B; line segments AD and BC are parallel, BD is the diagonal from B to D, DC connects from D to C; there is a right-angle mark at A. Reasoning: From the problem it is given that AD ∥ BC, ∠BAD = 90°, BD ⟂ DC, so ∠BDC = 90°. Consider triangles ADB and DBC. Because AD ∥ BC, and BD is a transversal, ∠ADB = ∠DBC. Also because ∠BAD = ∠BDC = 90°, therefore △ADB ∼ △DBC. From the corresponding-side relationship, AD/BD = BD/BC can be obtained. Substituting AD = 4, BC = 9, gives BD² = 4 × 9 = 36, so BD = 6.
